subject.title: Externally-registered cron jobs auto-enable without user confirmation, inherit expensive default model, no usage circuit breaker

question: What default security policy should OpenClaw enforce before externally, plugin, or agent-registered recurring agentTurn cron jobs can run on an inherited provider model?
rationale: The source repro is clear, but the fix changes persistent scheduling defaults, plugin scheduling contracts, model/provider cost policy, and upgrade behavior, so automation should not choose the boundary unilaterally.

options.title: Coordinated Cron Safety Policy
options.body: Require operator-visible activation or approval for new recurring external/plugin agentTurn jobs and pair it with explicit model-cost visibility plus doctor/update migration guidance.

options.title: Narrow Model-Cost Guard
options.body: Keep current activation behavior but warn or block recurring agentTurn jobs that inherit an expensive default model without an explicit job model.

options.title: Split Into RFC Follow-Ups
options.body: Use #71712 for provenance, #42475 for budgets, and #14376 for circuit breakers while keeping this issue as the consent/default-model cluster index.

recommendation.title: Coordinated Cron Safety Policy
recommendation.body: Require operator-visible activation or approval for new recurring external/plugin agentTurn jobs and pair it with explicit model-cost visibility plus doctor/update migration guidance.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent has the strongest current-source and recent-history connection to the cron model-selection, default, and plugin scheduling paths that would need coordinated policy changes.
